# RFID Access Control

> Manage employee access control


## What this module does

Manage employee access control.

This guide is for users who **configure** and **use** the module. If you need to install, upgrade, integrate or extend it, see the technical reference in [`llms-full.md`](llms-full.md).


## How to configure

Open **Settings → General Settings** and look for the section named after this module. Available options:

- **Event life time** — Number of days to keep access events in the system. Events older than this will be automatically deleted to save storage space. Default is 365 days (1 year).
- **Accept new Modules** — Allow the system to automatically register new hardware modules when they connect. Enable this when adding new controllers to your system. Disable for security after all modules are registered. Note: Does not support Multi-Company setups.
- **Debug JSON communication** — Save all communication between the system and hardware controllers to logs. Only enable this for troubleshooting hardware issues. It creates large log files and should be disabled during normal operation.
- **Time & Attendance control** — Enable time tracking features using RFID cards. Employees can check in/out by scanning their cards at designated readers.
- **Time & Attendance additional calculations** — Add advanced attendance calculations like late arrivals, early departures, and overtime tracking to the basic time & attendance features.
- **Vending Control** — Control vending machines with RFID cards. Allows employees to purchase items from vending machines using their access cards.
- **Realtime Dashboards** — Display live dashboards showing current access activity, who's in each area, and real-time security monitoring.
- **PMS Base functionality** — Property Management System integration. Allows using RFID system for hotel room access and guest management.
- **Andromeda Import** — Import data from Andromeda access control systems. Use this to migrate from an existing Andromeda installation.


## How to use it

### Real-time connection (instant commands)

By default a module picks up its commands on its next check-in, which can take
up to a minute. The real-time connection keeps the module permanently linked
to the system, so commands (open a door, update a card, set the clock) reach
it within seconds - even when the module is behind NAT or a firewall.

- **Automatic for the newest modules**: an iCON1XX 100.1 module turns the
  real-time connection on by itself the first time it is discovered - nothing
  to press. Older modules use **Enable real-time** (Access Control -> Modules,
  "Real-time connection" section). Either way the module receives its
  connection settings on its next check-in - nothing to configure on the device.
- **Online badge**: "Real-time Online" shows whether the module is currently
  connected. "Last Real-time Activity" is the last moment it was heard from.
- **Accept new key** (officers only): use it after you change the module's
  security key on the device itself - the module's next check-in then registers
  the new key with the system.
- **Disable real-time** returns the module to the classic check-in mode.
- The classic communication keeps working at all times: if the real-time
  connection drops, the module falls back automatically and no events are
  lost.

Requirement: the server must be reachable over HTTPS in production and run
with a websocket (gevent) port - see the technical reference for deployment
notes.

### When the screens update, and when they stay quiet

The monitoring screens refresh by themselves when something happens that an
operator would act on: a badge at a door, a zone in alarm, a refused command, a
module that went dark or came back, or any change someone makes in Odoo.

They deliberately do NOT refresh for device housekeeping. A module checks in
about once a minute and a controller reports its status every five minutes;
those messages repeat the same picture, and repainting the screen for each of
them was the single largest source of traffic in the system - on a 176-module
site, roughly half a million updates a day, enough to overwhelm the real-time
connection. The data is still recorded; only the pointless refresh is dropped.

**Module presence.** A module that stops reporting cannot tell anyone - so the
system checks for itself every five minutes. A module that has been silent for
more than ten minutes counts as a miss, and after three misses in a row it is
reported as no longer reachable: the list and the cards turn from green to
orange. The tolerance exists because only modules Odoo set up itself are
guaranteed to report every minute - one configured by hand on the device may
report more slowly, and a single missed check-in must not paint it orange.
Coming back is not delayed by any of this: the very first check-in turns it
green again at once. Modules on the real-time connection are judged by that
connection, not by the older check-in timestamp, so a healthy real-time module
is never reported as dark.

Note this corrects a long-standing defect: until now the indicator only ever
turned green and never back, so a module that had gone dark still looked healthy.

### Sharing a module between companies

One physical module can serve two (or more) companies at the same time - for
example two schools sharing one building entrance. The module always has ONE
owner company; the "Shared With" field on the module form lists the other
companies that use it.

- **What the sharing companies get**: they SEE the controllers, doors and
  readers of the module, and can add its doors to their OWN access groups to
  give access to their OWN people. System events of the module (forced door,
  power loss, unknown card) are visible to every company using it. They cannot
  change the hardware itself - configuring, moving or deleting controllers and
  doors, and the command queue, stay with the owner company (the queue lists
  the owner's card numbers and PIN codes).
- **The module record stays private to the owner**: it holds the device
  credentials that let the hardware sign in, so it is never shown to the
  sharing companies. They work with the doors and readers instead.
- **What stays private**: cards, access groups, schedules, work codes and
  people are never shared. Each company sees only its own people's access
  events - even on a shared door.
- **Ownership stays with the owner**: only the owner company (or a system
  administrator) can change the owner, change the sharing list or delete the
  module.
- **Setting it up**: adding a company to "Shared With" requires a user who can
  see both companies (typically the administrator serving both). The owner
  company can always REMOVE a company from the list on its own - the removed
  company's access rights on the module's doors are revoked automatically.
- **Card numbers on a shared module**: people from the sharing companies must
  carry different card numbers on the shared doors - the hardware stores only
  the number, so a duplicate would make the events ambiguous. The system
  refuses such a duplicate at the moment access is granted and tells you which
  number collides.
- **Time schedules**: a sharing company grants access with the unrestricted
  (24/7) schedule. Time-limited access on a shared module is configured by the
  owner company.


### HR RFID Access Control

[![License: AGPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-AGPL%20v3-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0)
[![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/Version-19.0.2.2.1-green.svg)](https://apps.odoo.com)

The main RFID Access Control module for Odoo, providing comprehensive hardware integration and access management capabilities.

#### 🎯 Overview

HR RFID is the core module of the Polimex RFID Suite, offering enterprise-grade access control management integrated with Odoo's HR system. It supports various RFID controllers and provides real-time monitoring, advanced access rules, and comprehensive reporting.

#### ✨ Key Features

##### Hardware Management
- **Multi-Controller Support**: iCON50, iCON110, iCON115, iCON130, iCON180
- **Webstack Communication**: HTTP-based controller management
- **Real-time Events**: Live event processing and monitoring
- **Hardware Discovery**: Automatic detection of controllers on network

##### Access Control
- **Access Groups**: Define who can access which doors
- **Time Schedules**: Configure access based on time periods
- **Zone Management**: Group doors into logical zones
- **Emergency Groups**: Special access during emergencies
- **Anti-passback**: Prevent card sharing and enforce area occupancy

##### Card Management
- **Multiple Card Types**: RFID, Barcode, PIN support
- **Card Lifecycle**: Issue, activate, deactivate, expire
- **Bulk Operations**: Import/export card data
- **Card Templates**: Predefined card configurations

##### Security Features
- **Duress PIN**: Silent alarm triggering
- **Alarm Management**: Door forced, door open too long
- **Audit Trail**: Complete event logging
- **Multi-Company**: Data isolation between companies

##### Integration
- **HR Integration**: Link cards to employees
- **Partner Integration**: Visitor and contractor management
- **Event Webhooks**: External system notifications
- **REST API**: For third-party integrations

#### 📋 Requirements

- Odoo 18.0+
- Python 3.8+
- PostgreSQL 12+
- Compatible RFID hardware

##### Python Dependencies
```
- Standard Odoo dependencies
```

##### Odoo Dependencies
- `base`
- `mail`
- `hr`
- `digest`

#### 🛠️ Installation

1. Copy the module to your Odoo addons directory:
```bash
cp -r hr_rfid /path/to/odoo/addons/
```

2. Update the module list:
```bash
./odoo-bin -d your_database -u hr_rfid
```

3. Install via Odoo Apps interface or command line:
```bash
./odoo-bin -d your_database -i hr_rfid
```

#### 🔧 Configuration

##### Initial Setup

1. **System Parameters**
   - Navigate to Settings → Technical → System Parameters
   - Configure `hr_rfid.*` parameters as needed

2. **Webstack Configuration**
   - Go to RFID → Configuration → Webstacks
   - Add your webstack with IP and port
   - Test connection using the "Test" button

3. **Controller Setup**
   - Controllers will auto-appear after webstack connection
   - Configure each controller's settings
   - Map readers to doors

4. **Access Groups**
   - Create access groups under RFID → Access Groups
   - Define time schedules if needed
   - Assign doors to groups

##### Hardware Setup

###### Network Configuration
```
Webstack Default Port: 80
Controller Communication: HTTP
Event Endpoint: /hr/rfid/event
```

###### Controller Types
- **iCON50**: 1 door, 1 readers
- **iCON110**: 1-2 door, 2 readers, IO support
- **iCON115**: 1-2 door, 2 readers, IO support, alarm support
- **iCON130**: 2-4 doors, 4 readers, IO support
- **turnstile**: 1 doors, 4 readers, IO support with specific turnstile features
- **iCON180**: 4 doors, 8 readers, IO support, alarm support
- **Relay**: up to 512 door, 2 readers, IO support with relays for elevator control and etc.
- **Fire**: IO support with fire alarm control panel with 4 analog fire line inputs
- **iTemp**: up to 90 temperature sensors, IO support with temperature monitoring

#### 📖 Usage

##### Managing Cards

1. **Issue New Card**
   - Go to RFID → Cards → Create
   - Enter card number (or scan)
   - Assign to employee/partner
   - Select access groups

2. **Bulk Import**
   - RFID → Cards → Import
   - Use Excel template provided
   - Map columns and import

##### Monitoring Access

1. **Live Events**
   - RFID → Events → User Events
   - Real-time event stream
   - Filter by door, person, or time

2. **Door Status**
   - RFID → Doors
   - View current door states
   - Remote open/close doors

##### Reports

- Access logs by person
- Door usage statistics
- Failed access attempts
- Alarm history

#### 🔌 API Reference

##### Event Processing
```python
### Event endpoint: /hr/rfid/event
POST /hr/rfid/event
{
    "controller_id": "ctrl_serial",
    "event_type": "card_read",
    "reader_id": 1,
    "card_number": "1234567890",
    "timestamp": "2024-01-01 12:00:00"
}
```

##### Remote Commands
```python
### Open door remotely
door.remote_open(user_id)

### Add card to controller
card.add_to_controllers()

### Emergency open all doors
access_group.emergency_open()
```

#### 🐛 Troubleshooting

##### Common Issues

1. **Webstack not connecting**
   - Check network connectivity
   - Verify firewall rules
   - Confirm webstack service is running

2. **Cards not working**
   - Verify card is active
   - Check access group assignments
   - Confirm time schedules

3. **Events not appearing**
   - Check controller online status
   - Verify event processing cron job
   - Review system logs

### In configuration
log_level = debug
log_handler = hr_rfid:DEBUG
```

### Available actions

- **Set active**
- **Set inactive**
- **Set webstack settings** — Set webstack settings for the module.
- **Check if ws available**
- **Close panel rfid setup**
- **Fetch rfid onboarding** — Fetch RFID onboarding step data for the frontend banner.
- **Open step rfid settings**
- **Open step add webstack**
- **Open step scan controllers**
- **Open step create access group**
- **Open step register card**
- **Send badge email** — Open a window to compose an email, with the template - 'card_badge'


## Common questions and errors

Actions in this list display a message dialog when something is wrong (missing data, invalid configuration, server unreachable, etc.). If an action fails, read the dialog message and check the configuration described above.

- **Set webstack settings** (on `hr.rfid.webstack`) — Set webstack settings for the module.
- **Check if ws available** (on `hr.rfid.webstack`)
